title: Rational fixed vectors for arbitrary unitriangular subgroup schemes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $U$ be an affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose there are $n\geq1$ and a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of group schemes $U\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_{n,k}$, where $\mathcal U_{n,k}(A)$ consists of upper triangular $n\times n$ matrices with diagonal entries $1$, with matrix multiplication, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Let $d\geq1$ and let $\rho:U\to\operatorname{GL}_{d,k}$ be a homomorphism of group schemes, a rational representation [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Then there exists $0\ne v\in k^d$ such that, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and every $u\in U(A)$, $\rho_A(u)(1\otimes v)=1\otimes v$ in $A\otimes_k k^d$. No smoothness, reducedness, connectedness, perfectness or characteristic assumption is made.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(b) implies (a), printed pp.281–282; the definition preceding Proposition 14.3, printed p.280: fixed vector means invariant for the rational representation, not only for k-points.

proof.text:
Put $P=k[x_{ij}:1\leq i<j\leq n]$. Giving a $k$-algebra map $P\to R$ is exactly giving all strictly upper entries of a unitriangular matrix over $R$, naturally in $R$. Thus $\mathcal U_{n,k}=\operatorname{Spec}P$. The matrix multiplication formula on the universal pair of matrices gives
$$\Delta_P(x_{ij})=x_{ij}\otimes1+1\otimes x_{ij}+\sum_{i<l<j}x_{il}\otimes x_{lj},\qquad\epsilon_P(x_{ij})=0.$$
These are the coordinate Hopf maps, and $\Delta_P$ preserves products and units.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(b) implies (c), printed p.281, equation (92): coordinate presentation and multiplication formula.

proof.text:
Assign $x_{ij}$ weight $j-i$ and let $F_r\subseteq P$ be the span of monomials of weight at most $r$. Positive weights imply $F_0=k1$; every polynomial is a finite sum of monomials, so $\bigcup_rF_r=P$. In each term of $\Delta_P(x_{ij})$ the two weights add to $j-i$, including $(l-i)+(j-l)=j-i$. Expanding the product of these expressions for a monomial of weight $s$ gives only tensors of monomials with weights $a,b$ satisfying $a+b=s$. If $s\leq r$, each such term lies in $F_a\otimes F_{r-a}$. By linearity,
$$\Delta_P(F_r)\subseteq\sum_{a=0}^rF_a\otimes F_{r-a}.$$
For $n=1$, $P=k$ and $F_r=k$ for every $r$.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(b) implies (c), printed p.281, weight assignment following (92) and its monomial-product calculation.

proof.text:
Write $B=k[U]$. The given closed immersion into $\operatorname{Spec}P$ induces a surjective $k$-algebra map $q:P\twoheadrightarrow B$. Compatibility of the immersion with multiplication and identity gives $\Delta_Bq=(q\otimes q)\Delta_P$ and $\epsilon_Bq=\epsilon_P$. Set $C_r=q(F_r)$. These subspaces are increasing and exhaustive by surjectivity, $C_0=k1_B$, and applying $q\otimes q$ to the inclusion in step 2 gives
$$\Delta_B(C_r)\subseteq\sum_{a=0}^r C_a\otimes C_{r-a}.$$
Moreover $\Delta_B(1_B)=1_B\otimes1_B$ and $\epsilon_B(1_B)=1$. In particular $1_B\ne0$, since the counit takes it to $1\in k$.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(b) implies (c), printed p.281, first sentence: pass to the image filtration in the coordinate quotient; Stacks Tag 01QO, affine closed immersions, as explicitly included in def-weil-closed-immersion.

proof.text: Let $V=k^d$. The representation-comodule dictionary applied to the given affine finite-type group scheme $U$ and homomorphism $\rho$ supplies $c:V\to V\otimes_kB$ with $(c\otimes1)c=(1\otimes\Delta_B)c$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon_B)c=1_V$. The coalgebra of $B$, the filtration $C_r$ of step 3, and $g=1_B$ satisfy every hypothesis of the filtered-coalgebra lemma. Since $d\geq1$, $V\ne0$. Applying that lemma yields $0\ne v\in k^d$ with $c(v)=v\otimes1_B$.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(c) implies (a), printed pp.281–282; Remark 4.1, equations (24)–(25), printed p.84, for conversion to the comodule.

proof.text: For every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and every $u\in U(R)$, let $x:B\to R$ be its algebra map. The dictionary's evaluation formula sends $c(v)=v\otimes1_B$ to $\rho_R(u)(v\otimes1)=v\otimes x(1_B)=v\otimes1$. Under the tensor flip $v\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes v$, whose inverse is the same flip, this is precisely $\rho_R(u)(1\otimes v)=1\otimes v$ in $R\otimes_k k^d$. The chosen nonzero vector is over $k$ and works for all $R,u$.

source.place: Definition preceding Proposition 14.3, printed p.280; Remark 4.1, printed p.84, evaluation formula for the rational action, not merely k-points.
